design:
1. Where it lives. A project's sessions are a project tab named Sessions, the first entry behind More ▾ (Sessions, Plan, Docs, Reviews, Costs, Data), at /projects/:id/sessions (the address that today falls back to the Overview). No new primary tab and nothing new on Home: the list is looked back on, not part of the loop's five daily things (design §1, §6). It is one click from the two places a person thinks of sessions: the Overview's Last result gains 'All 14 sessions' next to 'Open the session' (shown from two sessions on), and every session page gains 'All sessions' next to 'Open the project'.
2. The page. One heading line: '14 sessions · CHF 4.20 in all'. On top, the session working now (normally one; several only on a shared project in wave 8), with a pulsing dot. Below it, the ended sessions, newest first by when they began, 20 at a time, and at the end a 'Show older sessions' button that adds the next 20 (keyset paging, so a session that starts meanwhile never shifts or repeats a row). Under the list, when chat about this project cost anything: 'Chat about this project: CHF 0.30.' with Open Chat. Empty: 'No sessions yet. Each session is listed here with what it did and what it cost.'
3. One row, two lines; the whole row opens the session's page. Line 1, what it did, one sentence of at most 100 characters (design §5): 'Did 3 tasks: "Create index.html", "Style the page" and "Add the README".', '"Long report" paused at its budget of CHF 0.40.', '"Write the scope" failed.', '"Decide where the page is published" needed your answer.', 'You cancelled "Draft the FAQ"; nothing else ran.', 'Nothing finished.'; a planning session: 'Drafted a plan of 5 tasks; you approved it.' (or '; it waits for your approval.', '; you asked for changes.', '; you rejected it.'), 'Planning failed: Claude did not answer (network).'. Line 2, small: when · how long · the tasks · how it ended · the money: '14:05 · 12 min · 3 done, 1 failed · Stopped by you · CHF 0.80 on your API key' ('8 Nov, 09:12' on another day; 'under a minute'; '1 h 5 min'). The task counts are the session's as it ended (done, paused, failed, needed you), only those above zero. How it ended uses the session page's own words (one map), with the two present-tense states said in the past for an ended session: 'Stopped to wait for a Claude credential', 'Ended with a plan for you to approve'; 'Ended: 1 task needs you' stays true now. A planning row says how it ended only when it was stopped, interrupted or failed. The money is the session's one figure, with whose credential paid: 'on your API key', 'of your Claude subscription's allowance', 'of your plan credits', 'on your API key and your Claude subscription' when both paid, nothing more on the stand-in; under a centime 'less than CHF 0.01'. A session that did not start from a plain Start says why, after the time: 'started by itself when Claude could work again', 'started on its schedule', 'started by a pull request comment', 'started by CI', 'started from your phone'.
4. The working row: line 1 is the project's working sentence ('Working on "Style the page" (3 of 7 done)', 'Choosing the next task…', 'Stopping after this task', 'Starting…', 'Drafting the plan…'); line 2 'Started 14:05 · 12 min · CHF 0.40 so far on your API key'. The elapsed time ticks; the task, progress and money follow the live stream (a re-read on the project's change and on the session's frames, at most once per 5 s). There is no Stop on the row: Stop lives on the session page and in the header (one place per action); the row opens the page.
5. What is listed: every session of the project that ran a task, spent money, or is working now: work sessions however they started, each planning call (every 'Change the plan' redraft is one), interrupted ones. Not listed: the chat's conversation (the one line at the bottom), sessions without a project (the critic's calibration), and a session that ended without running a task and without spending anything (design §4.8: nothing runnable is no session; it would be noise from automatic starts). Every CHF a session spent is therefore in exactly one row, and 'in all' is the sum of the rows.
6. A click opens the session's page. Its header gains 'All sessions'. A planning session's page is titled 'Quote page · planning at 14:05', its status reads 'Drafting the plan', 'Plan drafted' or 'Planning failed', and its result is the planning sentence, never 'intake: …'. Every session page gains 'Tasks in this session' above the log: one row per task it worked on, in the order it started them, with the title (opens the task drawer, /projects/:id/tasks?task=<id>), what happened to it in this session (Done, Failed, Paused at its budget of CHF 0.40, Needed your answer, Cancelled by you, Stopped before it finished, Being reviewed when it ended), 'now: Done' when its status has changed since (design §2 words, true now), and what this session spent on it. Then the log as today. 'Spent of this session's budget' shows the same figure as the list row.
7. One figure per session, everywhere: the cost ledger's CHF sum for the session as booked (ADR 0008, U-074). The list row, the session page and the Overview's Last result read the same amount, after a change of the day's rate, after a restart, and after a stopped run's late booking.
8. Behind it: GET /projects/:id/sessions?before=<cursor>&limit=<n> (20 by default, at most 50) answers the working rows, one page of ended rows, the cursor of the next page, the count and the CHF in all, and the chat line, all words computed by the daemon (ADR 0102: the phone later shows the same). GET /sessions/:id/tasks answers the session page's task rows. GET /sessions keeps its shape (the running poller and the phone use it); its planning rows get words instead of 'intake: …' and its spend becomes the one figure. What each session did is written on its own row when it ends (handoff.outcome from the runner and from recovery, handoff.planning when a planning call closes), so the list reads the same after a restart; rows written before run C fall back to the handoff's id lists. An interrupted session's length ends at its last logged step, not at the recovery.
alternatives_rejected: A primary Sessions tab next to Overview, Tasks, Chat and Files: design §6 keeps four primary tabs for the daily loop; a history is looked back on. Behind More plus the links from Last result and from every session page it is still one click from where a person looks for it.

An 'Earlier sessions' block on the Overview: the Overview's job is where the project stands now, with Last result capped at three lines (§3.4); a history there makes the screen long and repeats the session pages.

Sessions inside the Costs tab (a 'By session' table): Costs answers where money went by model, specialist and task; a person asking 'what did yesterday's session do and how did it end' would not look there, and the row's sentence is not a cost.

A Sessions screen across all projects behind the top More: the owner asked for each project's list; one project's history is what a person reads. The same route can feed a cross-project list later without a new design.

Reusing GET /sessions?projectId=: it returns raw rows (the stored three-line result with its own CHF, 'intake: …' for planning rows, the raw handoff, the spend at today's rate), the newest 100 and no paging; the running poller and the phone depend on its shape. A project-scoped route with the daemon's words also falls under wave 8's /projects/:id* ownership middleware.
Showing each session's stored three-line result in its row: too long for a row and the same paragraph in two places (§5.10 one place per fact); the row has one sentence, the page has the result.

Recomputing what an old session did from its log on every read: slow on a long history and fragile across log changes; the record is written once on the row at the end, and old rows fall back to the handoff's id lists.
Chat as sessions (one per turn or per day): the chat is one conversation per project (§3.9), not sessions; one line with its cost and Open Chat is enough to make its spend visible.
Infinite scroll: a 'Show older sessions' button is predictable, keyboard-friendly and testable; 20 rows cover weeks of work.
A Stop button on the working row: a second place to stop invites a mis-click on a list; Stop stays on the session page and in the header (design §3.1, §3.7).

Listing every session row, including those that ran nothing and spent nothing: automatic starts after answers or credential wakes can end at once with nothing runnable (§4.8); they would fill the list with 'Nothing could run'. Any session that spent money is listed, so no spend is hidden.

Saying 'CHF 0.80 on your Claude subscription': it reads as a charge; the subscription is measured against its allowance in CHF of API-equivalent use (Settings), so 'of your Claude subscription's allowance' is the true sentence.

decisions: Place: Sessions is the first entry behind More ▾ (Sessions, Plan, Docs, Reviews, Costs, Data), at /projects/:id/sessions; the Overview's Last result links 'All N sessions' from two sessions on, and every session page links 'All sessions'. Why: design §6 keeps four primary tabs for the daily loop; the list is looked back on; one click from the two places a person thinks of sessions; no clutter on Home or the Overview.

A row is two lines and one link: the gist sentence first (≤ 100 characters, design §5), then 'when · how long · task counts · how it ended · CHF on which credential' (and 'started by itself …' when not a plain Start). Why: exactly what the owner listed (what each did, spent, how it ended), read at a glance; the full result stays on the session page (§5.10).

The working session(s) sit above the list with live progress, using the project's working sentence ('Working on "Style the page" (3 of 7 done)') and 'CHF … so far'; no Stop on the row. Why: one status map (§2); Stop lives on the session page and the header (§3.1, §3.7).

Order: newest first by start (created_at, then id); 20 a page, at most 50; 'Show older sessions' with an opaque keyset cursor. Why: a session starting meanwhile never shifts or repeats rows; a cursor stays valid across a restart.

Listed: every session of the project that ran a task, spent money or works now, planning calls included; not the conversation, not sessions without a project, not a session that ended without running a task and without spending. Why: every CHF a session spent is in exactly one row and 'in all' is their sum; automatic starts that found nothing (§4.8) are not news.

Chat is one line under the list, 'Chat about this project: CHF 0.30.' with Open Chat, only when above zero. Why: chat is one conversation, not sessions (§3.9), but its spend about the project must be visible (D3 lets it grow).

One figure per session: the cost ledger's CHF sum for the session as booked, used by the list row, by SessionView.spent (the session page's 'Spent of this session's budget') and already by the result sentence; a late booking that lands after the result was written updates the row's spend and the result's cost sentence (confirm first). Why: ADR 0008 and U-074 (what the person reads is CHF from the ledger's own conversion); two amounts for one session is a contradiction.

Credential words: 'CHF 0.80 on your API key', 'CHF 0.80 of your Claude subscription's allowance', 'CHF 0.80 of your plan credits', 'CHF 0.80 on your API key and your Claude subscription' when both paid; no credential words on the stand-in; moneyWords for amounts under a centime. Why: Settings measures a subscription against its allowance in CHF of API-equivalent use; 'on your subscription' would read as a charge.

The record: at its end each session writes handoff.outcome (the named LastSessionOutcome: done, failed with reasons, needs_you, paused with limit words, cancelled, released) on its own row, from the runner and from recovery; a planning call writes handoff.planning (its failure words, through redact and withoutIds) when it closes; the plan's size and fate are read from the plan card whose session_id is the row's. Rows from before run C fall back to handoff.done and handoff.blocked ('2 left for you'). Why: the list must read the same after a restart and after later sessions, without re-deriving it from logs.

How it ended: one map, the session page's (sessionStatusText/endedStatusText), with past tense for an ended session's two present-tense states ('Stopped to wait for a Claude credential', 'Ended with a plan for you to approve'); 'Ended: 1 task needs you' stays true now. A planning row says how it ended only when stopped, interrupted or failed; its page reads 'Drafting the plan', 'Plan drafted', 'Planning failed'. Why: §5 rule 4 true now; one map for the badge and the row.
An interrupted session's duration ends at its last logged event before the recovery's own session.ended line. Why: the downtime is not the session's length.

The session page gains 'Tasks in this session' (title opening the drawer, what happened here, 'now: …' when different, CHF this session spent on it) and 'All sessions'; GET /sessions/:id/tasks serves it. Why: the owner's 'each opening the session's page', with its tasks and log; U-086.

Routes: GET /projects/:id/sessions and GET /sessions/:id/tasks are new; GET /sessions keeps its shape (summary words for planning rows, spend as the one figure). All words are the daemon's. Why: the running poller and the phone use GET /sessions; a project route fits wave 8's ownership middleware; ADR 0102 (the phone shows the daemon's words).

startedBy words for any trigger but a plain Start: 'started by itself when Claude could work again' (budget_reset), 'started on its schedule' (schedule), 'started by a pull request comment', 'started by CI', 'started from your phone'; an answer's or an approval's start (message) and a plain Start say nothing. Why: sessions that start by themselves (D4, credential waits) must say so; a start from the person's own click is not repeated (§5.11).
